You are reverse-engineering the behavior of a compiled binary at /workspace/executable (call it as ./executable from /workspace).
It is "gomplate", a Go text/template renderer. Documentation lives in /workspace/docs/content/.

HARD RULES (violating them fails the whole project):
- You MUST NOT use the network, MUST NOT search the web, MUST NOT download or read the original gomplate source from anywhere.
- You MUST NOT decompile, disassemble, objdump, strace, ltrace, nm, strings(1), or otherwise statically analyze ./executable.
- You may ONLY run ./executable with normal CLI arguments and observe stdout/stderr/exit code, and read the bundled docs.

How to invoke: ./executable -i '<template>'   (prints rendered result to stdout)
Errors are logged to stderr as JSON: {"time":...,"level":"ERROR","msg":"","err":"..."} and exit code 1.
Useful trick: wrap results with printf "%T / %#v" to learn the concrete Go type a function returns, e.g.
  ./executable -i '{{ printf "%T" (conv.ToInt "5") }}'
Another: {{ test.Kind x }} and {{ test.IsKind "int" x }} reveal reflect kinds.

YOUR OUTPUT: write a thorough markdown spec file. Be exhaustive and precise: this spec is the ONLY thing a
separate implementer agent will see — they will not have access to the binary at first. Every fact must be
concrete and verified by an actual command you ran.

For EVERY function in your assigned area document:
1. Exact name(s) including aliases (verify each alias actually exists in THIS build — docs are stale, some
   documented functions were removed; e.g. conv.Bool does NOT exist here).
2. Exact parameter order and count, including variadic behavior and gomplate's "data is the LAST argument"
   pipeline convention. Verify by experiment, not by reading docs.
3. The concrete Go return type (use printf "%T").
4. Type coercion rules for inputs (what happens with int vs string vs float vs bool vs nil vs slice vs map).
5. Error messages VERBATIM (copy the exact "err" string), and whether it errors vs returns zero value.
6. Edge cases: empty string, empty slice, nil, negative numbers, unicode/multibyte, very large numbers,
   wrong arg count, wrong types.
7. At least 5-15 concrete verified examples per function in the form:
   | template | output |
   Use a fenced table or list. Copy outputs EXACTLY (including whitespace/newlines; note trailing newlines).

Finish the spec with a "GOTCHAS" section listing anything surprising an implementer would get wrong.
Do not summarize or truncate — length is good. Aim for a very detailed document.

YOUR ASSIGNED AREA: coll
Relevant docs: /workspace/docs/content/functions/coll.md (read it first to get the function list, then verify each against the binary).
Focus on Dict/Slice/Has/Keys/Values/Append/Prepend/Uniq/Flatten/Reverse/Sort/Merge/Pick/Omit/GroupBy/Index/JSONPath/JQ/Set/Unset. Sort: test mixed types, maps by key, structs. Merge: deep-merge precedence order (which wins?). Flatten with depth arg. Test JQ separately but note its dispatch here.

Write your spec to /tmp/spec/coll.md using the Write tool. Then reply with just a one-paragraph summary of what you covered and anything you could not determine.

4	  main:
5	    parent: functions
6	---
7	
8	These functions help manipulate and query collections of data, like lists (slices, or arrays) and maps (dictionaries).
9	
10	#### Implementation Note
11	For the functions that return an array, a Go `[]any` is returned, regardless of whether or not the
12	input was a different type.
13	
14	## `coll.Dict`
15	
16	**Alias:** `dict`
17	
18	Dict is a convenience function that creates a map with string keys.
19	Provide arguments as key/value pairs. If an odd number of arguments
20	is provided, the last is used as the key, and an empty string is
21	set as the value.
22	
23	All keys are converted to strings.
24	
25	This function is equivalent to [Sprig's `dict`](http://masterminds.github.io/sprig/dicts.html#dict)
26	function, as used in [Helm templates](https://helm.sh/docs/chart_template_guide/functions_and_pipelines/).
27	
28	For creating more complex maps, see [`data.JSON`](../data/#datajson) or [`data.YAML`](../data/#datayaml).
29	
30	For creating arrays, see [`coll.Slice`](#collslice).
31	
32	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
33	### Usage
34	
35	```
36	coll.Dict in...
37	```
38	
39	### Arguments
40	
41	| name | description |
42	|------|-------------|
43	| `in...` | _(required)_ The key/value pairs |
44	
45	### Examples
46	
47	```console
48	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Dict "name" "Frank" "age" 42 | data.ToYAML }}'
49	age: 42
50	name: Frank
51	$ gomplate -i '{{ dict 1 2 3 | toJSON }}'
52	{"1":2,"3":""}
53	```
54	```console
55	$ cat <<EOF| gomplate
56	{{ define "T1" }}Hello {{ .thing }}!{{ end -}}
57	{{ template "T1" (dict "thing" "world")}}
58	{{ template "T1" (dict "thing" "everybody")}}
59	EOF
60	Hello world!
61	Hello everybody!
62	```
63	
64	## `coll.Slice`
65	
66	Creates a slice (like an array or list). Useful when needing to `range` over a bunch of variables.
67	
68	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
69	### Usage
70	
71	```
72	coll.Slice in...
73	```
74	
75	### Arguments
76	
77	| name | description |
78	|------|-------------|
79	| `in...` | _(required)_ the elements of the slice |
80	
81	### Examples
82	
83	```console
84	$ gomplate -i '{{ range coll.Slice "Bart" "Lisa" "Maggie" }}Hello, {{ . }}{{ end }}'
85	Hello, Bart
86	Hello, Lisa
87	Hello, Maggie
88	```
89	
90	## `coll.GoSlice`
91	
92	This exposes the `slice` function from Go's [`text/template`](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template/#hdr-Functions)
93	package. Note that using `slice` will use the `coll.Slice` function instead,
94	which may not be desired.
95	For some background on this, see [this issue](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/issues/1461).
96	
97	Here is the upstream documentation:
98	
99	```
100	slice returns the result of slicing its first argument by the
101	remaining arguments. Thus "slice x 1 2" is, in Go syntax, x[1:2],
102	while "slice x" is x[:], "slice x 1" is x[1:], and "slice x 1 2 3"
103	is x[1:2:3]. The first argument must be a string, slice, or array.
104	```
105	
106	See the [Go language spec](https://go.dev/ref/spec#Slice_expressions) for
107	more details.
108	
109	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
110	### Usage
111	
112	```
113	coll.GoSlice item [indexes...]
114	```
115	
116	### Arguments
117	
118	| name | description |
119	|------|-------------|
120	| `item` | _(required)_ the string, slice, or array to slice |
121	| `indexes...` | _(optional)_ the indexes to slice the item by (0 to 3 arguments) |
122	
123	### Examples
124	
125	```console
126	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.GoSlice "hello world" 3 8 }}'
127	lo wo
128	```
129	
130	## `coll.Has`
131	
132	**Alias:** `has`
133	
134	Reports whether a given object has a property with the given key, or whether a given array/slice contains the given value. Can be used with `if` to prevent the template from trying to access a non-existent property in an object.
135	
136	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
137	### Usage
138	
139	```
140	coll.Has in item
141	```
142	
143	### Arguments
144	
145	| name | description |
146	|------|-------------|
147	| `in` | _(required)_ The object or list to search |
148	| `item` | _(required)_ The item to search for |
149	
150	### Examples
151	
152	```console
153	$ gomplate -i '{{ $l := coll.Slice "foo" "bar" "baz" }}there is {{ if has $l "bar" }}a{{else}}no{{end}} bar'
154	there is a bar
155	```
156	```console
157	$ export DATA='{"foo": "bar"}'
158	$ gomplate -i '{{ $o := data.JSON (getenv "DATA") -}}
159	{{ if (has $o "foo") }}{{ $o.foo }}{{ else }}THERE IS NO FOO{{ end }}'
160	bar
161	```
162	```console
163	$ export DATA='{"baz": "qux"}'
164	$ gomplate -i '{{ $o := data.JSON (getenv "DATA") -}}
165	{{ if (has $o "foo") }}{{ $o.foo }}{{ else }}THERE IS NO FOO{{ end }}'
166	THERE IS NO FOO
167	```
168	
169	## `coll.Index`
170	
171	Returns the result of indexing the given map, slice, or array by the given
172	key or index. This is similar to the built-in `index` function, but the
173	arguments are ordered differently for pipeline compatibility. Also this
174	function is more strict, and will return an error when trying to access a
175	non-existent map key.
176	
177	Multiple indexes may be given, for nested indexing.
178	
179	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
180	### Usage
181	
182	```
183	coll.Index indexes... in
184	```
185	```
186	in | coll.Index indexes...
187	```
188	
189	### Arguments
190	
191	| name | description |
192	|------|-------------|
193	| `indexes...` | _(required)_ The key or index |
194	| `in` | _(required)_ The map, slice, or array to index |
195	
196	### Examples
197	
198	```console
199	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Index "foo" (dict "foo" "bar") }}'
200	bar
201	```
202	```console
203	$ gomplate -i '{{ $m := json `{"foo": {"bar": "baz"}}` -}}
204	  {{ coll.Index "foo" "bar" $m }}'
205	baz
206	```
207	```console
208	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Slice "foo" "bar" "baz" | coll.Index 1 }}'
209	bar
210	```
211	
212	## `coll.JSONPath`
213	
214	**Alias:** `jsonpath`
215	
216	Extracts portions of an input object or list using a [JSONPath][] expression.
217	
218	Any object or list may be used as input. The output depends somewhat on the expression; if multiple items are matched, an array is returned.
219	
220	JSONPath expressions can be validated at https://jsonpath.com
221	
222	[JSONPath]: https://goessner.net/articles/JsonPath
223	
224	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
225	### Usage
226	
227	```
228	coll.JSONPath expression in
229	```
230	```
231	in | coll.JSONPath expression
232	```
233	
234	### Arguments
235	
236	| name | description |
237	|------|-------------|
238	| `expression` | _(required)_ The JSONPath expression |
239	| `in` | _(required)_ The object or list to query |
240	
241	### Examples
242	
243	```console
244	$ gomplate -i '{{ .books | jsonpath `$..works[?( @.edition_count > 400 )].title` }}' -c books=https://openlibrary.org/subjects/fantasy.json
245	[Alice's Adventures in Wonderland Gulliver's Travels]
246	```
247	
248	## `coll.JQ`
249	
250	**Alias:** `jq`
251	
252	Filters an input object or list using the [jq](https://stedolan.github.io/jq/) language, as implemented by [gojq](https://github.com/itchyny/gojq).
253	
254	Any JSON datatype may be used as input (NOTE: strings are not JSON-parsed but passed in as is).
255	If the expression results in multiple items (no matter if streamed or as an array) they are wrapped in an array.
256	Otherwise a single item is returned (even if resulting in an array with a single contained element).
257	
258	JQ filter expressions can be tested at https://jqplay.org/
259	
260	See also:
261	
262	- [jq manual](https://stedolan.github.io/jq/manual/)
263	- [gojq differences to jq](https://github.com/itchyny/gojq#difference-to-jq)
264	
265	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
266	### Usage
267	
268	```
269	coll.JQ expression in
270	```
271	```
272	in | coll.JQ expression
273	```
274	
275	### Arguments
276	
277	| name | description |
278	|------|-------------|
279	| `expression` | _(required)_ The JQ expression |
280	| `in` | _(required)_ The object or list to query |
281	
282	### Examples
283	
284	```console
285	$ gomplate \
286	   -i '{{ .books | jq `[.works[]|{"title":.title,"authors":[.authors[].name],"published":.first_publish_year}][0]` }}' \
287	   -c books=https://openlibrary.org/subjects/fantasy.json
288	map[authors:[Lewis Carroll] published:1865 title:Alice's Adventures in Wonderland]
289	```
290	
291	## `coll.Keys`
292	
293	**Alias:** `keys`
294	
295	Return a list of keys in one or more maps.
296	
297	The keys will be ordered first by map position (if multiple maps are given),
298	then alphabetically.
299	
300	See also [`coll.Values`](#collvalues).
301	
302	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
303	### Usage
304	
305	```
306	coll.Keys in...
307	```
308	```
309	in... | coll.Keys
310	```
311	
312	### Arguments
313	
314	| name | description |
315	|------|-------------|
316	| `in...` | _(required)_ the maps |
317	
318	### Examples
319	
320	```console
321	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Keys (dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2) }}'
322	[bar foo]
323	$ gomplate -i '{{ $map1 := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 -}}{{ $map2 := dict "baz" 3 "qux" 4 -}}{{ coll.Keys $map1 $map2 }}'
324	[bar foo baz qux]
325	```
326	
327	## `coll.Values`
328	
329	**Alias:** `values`
330	
331	Return a list of values in one or more maps.
332	
333	The values will be ordered first by map position (if multiple maps are given),
334	then alphabetically by key.
335	
336	See also [`coll.Keys`](#collkeys).
337	
338	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
339	### Usage
340	
341	```
342	coll.Values in...
343	```
344	```
345	in... | coll.Values
346	```
347	
348	### Arguments
349	
350	| name | description |
351	|------|-------------|
352	| `in...` | _(required)_ the maps |
353	
354	### Examples
355	
356	```console
357	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Values (dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2) }}'
358	[2 1]
359	$ gomplate -i '{{ $map1 := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 -}}{{ $map2 := dict "baz" 3 "qux" 4 -}}{{ coll.Values $map1 $map2 }}'
360	[2 1 3 4]
361	```

363	## `coll.Append`
364	
365	**Alias:** `append`
366	
367	Append a value to the end of a list.
368	
369	_Note that this function does not change the given list; it always produces a new one._
370	
371	See also [`coll.Prepend`](#collprepend).
372	
373	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
374	### Usage
375	
376	```
377	coll.Append value list...
378	```
379	```
380	list... | coll.Append value
381	```
382	
383	### Arguments
384	
385	| name | description |
386	|------|-------------|
387	| `value` | _(required)_ the value to add |
388	| `list...` | _(required)_ the slice or array to append to |
389	
390	### Examples
391	
392	```console
393	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Slice 1 1 2 3 | append 5 }}'
394	[1 1 2 3 5]
395	```

397	## `coll.Prepend`
398	
399	**Alias:** `prepend`
400	
401	Prepend a value to the beginning of a list.
402	
403	_Note that this function does not change the given list; it always produces a new one._
404	
405	See also [`coll.Append`](#collappend).

407	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_

411	coll.Prepend value list...
412	```

414	list... | coll.Prepend value

418	
419	| name | description |

422	| `list...` | _(required)_ the slice or array to prepend to |

431	## `coll.Uniq`
432	
433	**Alias:** `uniq`
434	
435	Remove any duplicate values from the list, without changing order.
436	
437	_Note that this function does not change the given list; it always produces a new one._
438	
439	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
440	### Usage
441	
442	```
443	coll.Uniq list
444	```
445	```
446	list | coll.Uniq
447	```
448	
449	### Arguments
450	
451	| name | description |
452	|------|-------------|
453	| `list` | _(required)_ the input list |
454	
455	### Examples
456	
457	```console
458	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Slice 1 2 3 2 3 4 1 5 | uniq }}'
459	[1 2 3 4 5]
460	```

462	## `coll.Flatten`
463	
464	**Alias:** `flatten`
465	
466	Flatten a nested list. Defaults to completely flattening all nested lists,
467	but can be limited with `depth`.
468	
469	_Note that this function does not change the given list; it always produces a new one._
470	
471	_Added in gomplate [v3.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.6.0)_
472	### Usage
473	
474	```
475	coll.Flatten [depth] list
476	```
477	```
478	list | coll.Flatten [depth]
479	```
480	
481	### Arguments
482	
483	| name | description |
484	|------|-------------|
485	| `depth` | _(optional)_ maximum depth of nested lists to flatten. Omit or set to `-1` for infinite depth. |
486	| `list` | _(required)_ the input list |
487	
488	### Examples
489	
490	```console
491	$ gomplate -i '{{ "[[1,2],[],[[3,4],[[[5],6],7]]]" | jsonArray | flatten }}'
492	[1 2 3 4 5 6 7]
493	```
494	```console
495	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Flatten 2 ("[[1,2],[],[[3,4],[[[5],6],7]]]" | jsonArray) }}'
496	[1 2 3 4 [[5] 6] 7]
497	```

499	## `coll.Reverse`
500	
501	**Alias:** `reverse`
502	
503	Reverse a list.
504	
505	_Note that this function does not change the given list; it always produces a new one._
506	
507	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
508	### Usage
509	
510	```
511	coll.Reverse list
512	```
513	```
514	list | coll.Reverse
515	```
516	
517	### Arguments
518	
519	| name | description |
520	|------|-------------|
521	| `list` | _(required)_ the list to reverse |
522	
523	### Examples
524	
525	```console
526	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Slice 4 3 2 1 | reverse }}'
527	[1 2 3 4]
528	```
529	
530	## `coll.Sort`
531	
532	**Alias:** `sort`
533	
534	Sort a given list. Uses the natural sort order if possible. For inputs
535	that are not sortable (either because the elements are of different types,
536	or of an un-sortable type), the input will simply be returned, unmodified.
537	
538	Maps and structs can be sorted by a named key.
539	
540	_Note that this function does not modify the input._
541	
542	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
543	### Usage
544	
545	```
546	coll.Sort [key] list
547	```
548	```
549	list | coll.Sort [key]
550	```
551	
552	### Arguments
553	
554	| name | description |
555	|------|-------------|
556	| `key` | _(optional)_ the key to sort by, for lists of maps or structs |
557	| `list` | _(required)_ the slice or array to sort |
558	
559	### Examples
560	
561	```console
562	$ gomplate -i '{{ coll.Slice "foo" "bar" "baz" | coll.Sort }}'
563	[bar baz foo]
564	```
565	```console
566	$ gomplate -i '{{ sort (coll.Slice 3 4 1 2 5) }}'
567	[1 2 3 4 5]
568	```
569	```console
570	$ cat <<EOF > in.json
571	[{"a": "foo", "b": 1}, {"a": "bar", "b": 8}, {"a": "baz", "b": 3}]
572	EOF
573	$ gomplate -d in.json -i '{{ range (include "in" | jsonArray | coll.Sort "b") }}{{ print .a "\n" }}{{ end }}'
574	foo
575	baz
576	bar
577	```
578	
579	## `coll.Merge`
580	
581	**Alias:** `merge`
582	
583	Merge maps together by overriding src with dst.
584	
585	In other words, the src map can be configured the "default" map, whereas the dst
586	map can be configured the "overrides".
587	
588	Many source maps can be provided. Precedence is in left-to-right order.
589	
590	_Note that this function does not modify the input._
591	
592	_Added in gomplate [v3.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.2.0)_
593	### Usage
594	
595	```
596	coll.Merge dst srcs...
597	```
598	```
599	srcs... | coll.Merge dst
600	```
601	
602	### Arguments
603	
604	| name | description |
605	|------|-------------|
606	| `dst` | _(required)_ the map to merge _into_ |
607	| `srcs...` | _(required)_ the map (or maps) to merge _from_ |
608	
609	### Examples
610	
611	```console
612	$ gomplate -i '{{ $default := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2}}
613	{{ $config := dict "foo" 8 }}
614	{{ merge $config $default }}'
615	map[bar:2 foo:8]
616	```
617	```console
618	$ gomplate -i '{{ $dst := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 }}
619	{{ $src1 := dict "foo" 8 "baz" 4 }}
620	{{ $src2 := dict "foo" 3 "bar" 5 }}
621	{{ coll.Merge $dst $src1 $src2 }}'
622	map[foo:1 bar:2 baz:4]
623	```
624	
625	## `coll.Pick`
626	
627	Given a map, returns a new map with any entries that have the given keys.
628	
629	The keys can either be separate arguments, or a slice (since v4.0.0).
630	
631	This is the inverse of [`coll.Omit`](#collomit).
632	
633	_Note that this function does not modify the input._
634	
635	_Added in gomplate [v3.7.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.7.0)_
636	### Usage
637	
638	```
639	coll.Pick keys... map
640	```
641	```
642	map | coll.Pick keys...
643	```
644	
645	### Arguments
646	
647	| name | description |
648	|------|-------------|
649	| `keys...` | _(required)_ the keys (strings) to match |
650	| `map` | _(required)_ the map to pick from |
651	
652	### Examples
653	
654	```console
655	$ gomplate -i '{{ $data := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 "baz" 3 }}
656	{{ coll.Pick "foo" "baz" $data }}'
657	map[baz:3 foo:1]
658	```
659	```console
660	$ gomplate -i '{{ $data := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 "baz" 3 }}
661	{{ $keys := coll.Slice "foo" "baz" }}
662	{{ coll.Pick $keys $data }}'
663	map[baz:3 foo:1]
664	```
665	
666	## `coll.Omit`
667	
668	Given a map, returns a new map without any entries that have the given keys.
669	
670	The keys can either be separate arguments, or a slice (since v4.0.0).
671	
672	This is the inverse of [`coll.Pick`](#collpick).
673	
674	_Note that this function does not modify the input._
675	
676	_Added in gomplate [v3.7.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.7.0)_
677	### Usage
678	
679	```
680	coll.Omit keys... map
681	```
682	```
683	map | coll.Omit keys...
684	```
685	
686	### Arguments
687	
688	| name | description |
689	|------|-------------|
690	| `keys...` | _(required)_ the keys (strings) to match |
691	| `map` | _(required)_ the map to omit from |
692	
693	### Examples
694	
695	```console
696	$ gomplate -i '{{ $data := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 "baz" 3 }}
697	{{ coll.Omit "foo" "baz" $data }}'
698	map[bar:2]
699	```
700	```console
701	$ gomplate -i '{{ $data := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 "baz" 3 }}
702	{{ $keys := coll.Slice "foo" "baz" }}
703	{{ coll.Omit $keys $data }}'
704	map[bar:2]
705	```
706	
707	## `coll.Set`
708	
709	**Alias:** `set`
710	
711	Sets the given key to the given value in the given map.
712	
713	The map is modified in place, and the modified map is returned.
714	
715	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
716	### Usage
717	
718	```
719	coll.Set key value map
720	```
721	```
722	map | coll.Set key value
723	```
724	
725	### Arguments
726	
727	| name | description |
728	|------|-------------|
729	| `key` | _(required)_ the key (string) to set |
730	| `value` | _(required)_ the value to set |
731	| `map` | _(required)_ the map to modify |
732	
733	### Examples
734	
735	```console
736	$ gomplate -i '{{ $data := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 }}
737	{{ coll.Set "baz" 3 $data }}'
738	map[bar:2 baz:3 foo:1]
739	```
740	```console
741	$ gomplate -i '{{ dict "foo" 1 | coll.Set "bar" 2 }}'
742	map[bar:2 foo:1]
743	```
744	
745	## `coll.Unset`
746	
747	**Alias:** `unset`
748	
749	Deletes the element with the specified key in the given map. If there is no such element, the map is returned unchanged.
750	
751	The map is modified in place, and the modified map is returned.
752	
753	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
754	### Usage
755	
756	```
757	coll.Unset key map
758	```
759	```
760	map | coll.Unset key
761	```
762	
763	### Arguments
764	
765	| name | description |
766	|------|-------------|
767	| `key` | _(required)_ the key (string) to unset |
768	| `map` | _(required)_ the map to modify |
769	
770	### Examples
771	
772	```console
773	$ gomplate -i '{{ $data := dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 "baz" 3 }}
774	{{ coll.Unset "bar" $data }}'
775	map[baz:3 foo:1]
776	```
777	```console
778	$ gomplate -i '{{ dict "foo" 1 "bar" 2 | coll.Unset "bar" }}'
779	map[foo:1]
780	```

input.command: ./executable --version; echo "---"; for f in coll.Dict dict coll.Slice coll.GoSlice coll.Has has coll.Index coll.JSONPath jsonpath coll.JQ jq coll.Keys keys coll.Values values coll.Append append coll.Prepend prepend coll.Uniq uniq coll.Flatten flatten coll.Reverse reverse coll.Sort sort coll.Merge merge coll.Pick coll.Omit coll.Set set coll.Unset unset coll.GroupBy groupBy coll.Group coll.Sort; do out=$(./executable -i "{{ printf \"%T\" $f }}" 2>&1); echo "$f => $out"; done

cat > /tmp/t.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: t.sh 'template'   -> prints "OUT: <stdout>" and "ERR: <err msg>" and exit code
cd /workspace
out=$(./executable -i "$1" 2>/tmp/err.txt)
rc=$?
err=$(cat /tmp/err.txt)
printf 'TPL: %s\n' "$1"
printf 'RC : %s\n' "$rc"
printf 'OUT: %q\n' "$out"
if [ -n "$err" ]; then
  # extract err field
  e=$(printf '%s' "$err" | sed -n 's/.*"err":"\(.*\)"}.*/\1/p')
  printf 'ERR: %s\n' "$e"
fi
echo '---'
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/t.sh
cat > /tmp/m.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# run many templates, one per line from stdin
while IFS= read -r line; do
  [ -z "$line" ] && continue
  /tmp/t.sh "$line"
done
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/m.sh
/tmp/t.sh '{{ printf "%T" (coll.Slice) }}'
